Subject: Performance gate review & hosted latency validation — Veridian

Hi Samantha — thanks again for a focused call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up a hosted evaluation: 

Recap of Veridian requirements from today's discovery:
- Primary SLO targets (end-to-end, client-facing): p95 ~ 120ms, p99 target ~ 400ms (you described a tight tail budget).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~180–220 reqs/s across peak window; concurrency burst up to ~60 concurrent inferences.
- Streaming: streaming partials for early token delivery is required for chat UX; goal is first partial within ~150ms of token generation and steady partial cadence thereafter.
- Payloads: average prompt + history ~1.6k tokens, 70% of calls are short (<=512 tokens).

Our asks / clarifying questions:
1) Can you confirm whether the target p99 (400ms) is measured end-to-end from client to client (including network and client-side processing) or just backend server-side?
2) Do you have a preferred 48–72 hour test window in Oct where you can route production-like traffic to our hosted endpoint?
3) Can you send sample request traces or a small baseline export (headers + timing) — helps us match batching & routing knobs.

Proposed Redwood-hosted target for test (we'll tune): p95 <= 140ms, p99 <= 420ms, target throughput 250 rps for safety during the test, concurrency cap 80 (configurable). We'll hand you a canary config to mirror your traffic shape.

Attached: veridian-test-plan.csv (traffic profile), hosted-latency-matrix-2025-10.xlsx (example matrix), redwood-canary-config.yaml (initial canary).

If that looks good, suggest we run a 48-hour test the week of Oct 20 — we can provision dedicated hosting for the window and share live dashboards. 

Thanks,
Chloe

Thanks Chloe — good write-up. A few clarifications from our side (quoting your bullets):

> Primary SLO targets (end-to-end, client-facing): p95 ~ 120ms, p99 target ~ 400ms

Those numbers are our client-facing expectations (i.e., measured from the browser through our edge and backend to the LLM response). Our current provider reports backend-only p95 ~ 100–115ms, p99 ~ 360–420ms depending on traffic; our observed end-to-end p99 has been ~430–480ms because of edge + network. Our hard requirement for go/no-go is end-to-end p99 <= 450ms.

> Streaming: streaming partials for early token delivery is required for chat UX; goal is first partial within ~150ms

Streaming is mandatory for chat flows. We need partials delivered with consistent cadence — spikes >250ms between partials are noticeable and hurt UX. gRPC streaming is our preferred transport but we can fall back to chunked HTTP if necessary.

We can do a 48-hour window Oct 20–21. I attached a small baseline export (veridian-current-baseline.jsonl) with request timestamps and sizes — sanitized but includes timing for request/response and edge hops.

One ask: can Redwood run the canary with a mode that preserves our edge headers for accurate end-to-end measurements? If not, we need to compensate in your dashboard.

Samantha Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops | Veridian AI
sruiz@veridian.ai

Internal notes / proposed test configuration (summary for Chloe to share):

1) Traffic profile: run two synthetic profiles during the 48h window — (A) steady ramp to 200rps with P95/99 sampling, (B) burst profile with 15s high-burst intervals to stress concurrency. Use veridian-test-plan.csv as shape.
2) Target SLAs to validate: hosted p95 <= 120–140ms (we'll attempt 120), hosted p99 <= 420ms (goal: demonstrate 400ms compatibility with their edge). These are backend-only; we will add an estimation layer to simulate their edge for end-to-end.
3) Streaming: implement gRPC streaming with early flush every 120–160ms. If gRPC not possible for certain clients, fallback to chunked-HTTP with identical flush cadence.
4) Canary config: redwood-canary-config.yaml will be the initial config. Key knobs to iterate during the run: kernel selection (int8/float fallback), batch size cap, kv-cache window, and continuous batching timeout (10–30ms).
5) Observability: provision dashboards with p95/p99 by route, tokenized cost, and per-token latency heatmaps.

Action items for Chloe: get PO/contact for procurement, confirm the edge-header preservation option, and ask Veridian to whitelist our test IPs.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
